details: AgentCard lists Stripe, Shopify, Square, Recurly, Razorpay, Braintree, Worldpay, Bambora and Mercado Pago; Square and the last four use prepared single-use checkout only. Adyen and VGS-backed wallets appear only in SDK notes. Matching endpoint, method, payload and complete aliases are still required.
A credential becoming consumed, or a timeout, does not prove an order was placed. Reconcile vault audit events with merchant order state before a repeat attempt.
Pricing table lists browser pools across plans; pricing FAQ limits them to Start-Up/Enterprise. Entitlement remains conditional pending account/provider confirmation.

The V4 schema describes secrets as usable without seeing them, but the 1Password guide explicitly notes that typed values can be accessible through the page/CDP. Record the narrower guarantee: secrets stay out of task text, not necessarily out of the entire agent environment.

V4 schema exposes agentcardWalletId and stripeLinkConnectionId. This verifies a native integration surface, not connected-wallet eligibility, per-site success, or identical credential-isolation design to Kernel.
API-key monthly caps are soft usage limits. They are not merchant spending caps. Auto recharge can charge immediately when enabled below the configured balance threshold.

Project request budget is max(25, 2 × concurrency) capped at 100 RPS (Free stays 25); status reads are uncapped max(25, 2 × concurrency). Edge WAF ceilings of 1,000/2,500 RPS per IP are separate. Docs put Tier 1 (50 sessions) at $100 while the pricing page says $200; trust the account limit.

Desktop operates approved local apps. Work cloud uses independent browser state. The API requires a developer runtime. Capabilities and permissions must not be transferred between these three surfaces by assumption.
General cloud browsing and authenticated browsing have different eligibility. Current docs say cloud sign-in is rolling out on Plus/Pro and unavailable for Enterprise/Edu.
Public product information is sparse. Purchase support has provider confirmation; exact CAPTCHA mechanisms, developer API, audit export, quotas, reliability and pricing remain unestablished.

Muse Secure VM is current. Meta's Sep 30 update still lists Shop Pay and 1Password as coming soon and Confidential VM as later this year. Shopify and PayPal posts are partner announcements, and Amazon blocks Muse (reported).

Current VM isolation does not cryptographically prevent Meta access. Training opt-out exists. Statements that VM data is not shared with ad systems do not mean merchant activity can never affect ad targeting.

No common task set, model configuration, site distribution or repeated trials across these products was executed. Published model/harness benchmarks cannot establish comparative purchase success here.
Instinct means instinct.com (Spear Street Technology); Meta means Muse, launched Sep 8. These are the likely matches to the request, not veterinary Instinct or other Meta research projects.

Cloud browsers, managed Agents and Stagehand v4 are separate columns. Hosted identity is conditional in local Stagehand; managed Agents own the model loop, while v4 removes agent() and requires external orchestration.

Stripe Issuing sample creates a virtual card with spend controls and fills checkout. This requires external Stripe access, not a documented native Link wallet. x402 payment for browser sessions must not be confused with merchant purchasing.
Managed Agents are explicitly outside ZDR and BYOS. Do not transfer enterprise browser infrastructure guarantees to managed Agents. BYO model key requires provider contact.

Solver docs describe default-on supported challenges; pricing lists automatic CAPTCHA solving on paid tiers. Keep plan eligibility conditional. hCaptcha-specific support was not established in reviewed documentation.

Functions are TypeScript-only, us-west-2-only, limited to 15 minutes, and have no persistent storage between invocations. Secrets are GA for Functions (Sep 30) but not documented for managed Agents. These limits are not assumed to be managed-Agent limits.

Browserbase / Stagehand added September 11, 2026. Refreshed October 5, 2026 from changelogs, releases and docs dated Sep 10–Oct 5; untouched entries keep earlier check dates. No hands-on tests were performed.
Kernel's Stagehand guide covers v4, running as an extension inside the Kernel browser, and v3. The September snapshot's v3-only statement was wrong.
us-east, eu-west and ap-southeast are on Start-Up and Enterprise. Regions reduce latency; profiles, replays and session metadata may be stored or processed in the US.
The Anthropic browser-toolset driver and V4 structured output are merged but in no released package (browser-use 0.13.10, SDK 3.11.3). Do not route on them until a release contains them.

Microsoft Copilot Autopilot is in private preview (reported Sep 25). On the Claude API, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 require computer_toolset_20260801; computer_20251124 returns 400 there. Neither is a column.

Desktop computer use, Work cloud browser, dots and Agents API computer use are separate products. Agents API computer use is a developer-run hosted browser billed by tokens and containers; it does not use ChatGPT sessions, saved logins or plan allowances.
/v1/agents is not ZDR-eligible: 30-day abuse-monitoring retention, application state kept until deleted, US data residency only. Not used for training.

dots docs do not mention purchases, spend limits or CAPTCHA solving; it shares Work's sign-in flow, but Work's payment behaviour is not assumed. Teams access is an invite-only alpha per the admin FAQ. Launch date is from press; the ChatGPT changelog has no dots entry.
